newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN CABLEWAY COMPANY CONSIDERS JSE LISTING.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN CABLEWAY COMPANY CONSIDERS JSE LISTING.

text.p: The firm which has taken tourists to the summit of Cape Town's landmark Table mountain for 70 years wants to join the heights of South Africa's economy and is considering a listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
Table Mountain Aerial Cableway (TMAC) managing director John Harrison said the company was thinking of going public.
This was not linked to financing a current 74 million rand upgrade, but to future projects elsewhere, he told Reuters.
A listing could be a means to finance one or more of the 11 cableway proposals put to his company over the past year.
"Listing would be an option...it's a question of getting the greatest value for the company," he said.

The existing cableway, which carried 450,000 people to the top of the 1,000-metre mountain last year, is 70 percent owned by Table Mountain Aerial Cableway Holdings and 30 percent by the families which helped to fund the original project in 1926.
Harrison said TMAC borrowed 50 million rand for the current upgrade, which would more than triple capacity.
"The balance will be funded internally and by means of a rights issue of around 14 million to 15 million rand," he said.

In terms of an agreement with the Cape Town City Council, TMAC will seek black participation in the rights issue as a way to broaden ownership of the cableway, which is among Cape Town's major tourist attractions.
"We are talking to representative black groupings in the Western Cape.... We're getting there," he said.

Harrison estimated that about half the proposals put to his company for new cableway projects in the Western Cape province, KwaZulu-Natal, the Johannesburg area and neighbouring countries were serious.
"Should we decide to list, this would be an ideal opportunity to raise the capital for these projects," he said.

The company was considering several options, including listing before the Cape Town cableway reopens in October, a share offer timed to coincide with the reopening or an offer after results are announced for the first six months of operations with the bigger cablecars.
The company, which has an accident-free record, announced a three million rand profit in the year to June on turnover of 9.5 million rand.
Harrison said the upgrade, including 65-person cablecars in place of the current 24-passenger models, would increase capacity from 230 people per hour to 900, substantially boosting turnover.
